author: Marisa Roman
title: There's A Historic Town In Colorado Where Mineral Water Bubbles Right Out Of The Ground, And You Need To Visit - NewsBreak
text:
By Marisa Roman ,
10 hours ago
Manitou Springs is six miles west of Colorado Springs and about a thousand feet above it, wedged into a narrow canyon between Garden of the Gods and Pikes Peak. You can walk it end-to-end in an afternoon, and most people who do it once come back.
The town was incorporated in 1888 on a single premise: that the naturally carbonated mineral water bubbling out of the ground here would make people well. Victorians arrived by the trainload to drink it. The health resort era faded, but the springs never stopped flowing, and you can still walk downtown and drink from eight of them for free.
What grew up around that is harder to categorize, and it is why USA Today’s 10Best named this one of the best small-town arts scenes in America . Here is what to actually do once you get here.
sfgamchick – Flickr Manitou Springs at a Glance Location: El Paso County, Colorado, about six miles west of downtown Colorado Springs Elevation: Roughly 6,300 feet in town. The base of the Manitou Incline sits at 6,530 feet and its summit at 8,550 feet Incorporated: 1888, founded as a scenic health resort Mineral springs: Eight free public fountains downtown, naturally carbonated, flowing 24 hours a day Signature hike: The Manitou Incline, 2,768 steps and 2,020 vertical feet. A free timed reservation is required Parking: Paid 7 a.m. to 6 p.m., free after 6 p.m. Downtown runs about $2 per hour in summer Nearest airport: Colorado Springs Airport, roughly 20 miles east Restaurants: More than 30 locally owned spots within three miles, per the local visitors bureau Biggest annual event: The Emma Crawford Coffin Races each October Things to Do in Manitou Springs Drink from the eight mineral springs This is the reason the town exists, and it costs nothing. Eight public fountains sit scattered through downtown, each fed by the same limestone aquifer and each tasting noticeably different. They run 24 hours a day. Start at the visitors bureau at 354 Manitou Avenue for a map and free tasting cups, then walk the loop.
Hike the Manitou Incline, or decide not to MelissaMN – stock.adobe.com The Incline is an old cable railway bed turned into a staircase: 2,768 railroad-tie steps climbing 2,020 vertical feet in under a mile, at an average grade of 41 percent. Roughly 250,000 people a year attempt it. You need a free, timed reservation booked in advance ; you cannot walk back down the steps, and the descent adds about 3 miles to the Barr Trail.
If that sounds like a lot, it is. The nearby Red Rock Canyon Open Space has eleven trails between 1.7 and 5.4 miles, with red rock scenery and only a fraction of the crowd.
Play the Penny Arcade At 930 Manitou Avenue, the Penny Arcade has been running since 1933. Admission is free, and you pay per machine, some of which still take actual pennies. It sprawls across eight connected buildings, holding more than 400 coin-operated games, from hand-cranked machines over a century old to Pac-Man and Galaga. Bring quarters.
MichaelVi – stock.adobe.com Ride the Cog Railway to the top of Pikes Peak The Broadmoor Manitou and Pikes Peak Cog Railway leaves from a depot on Ruxton Avenue and climbs to the 14,115-foot summit. The round trip runs about three hours, including 40 minutes at the top. It operates year-round, and the railway recommends booking about two weeks ahead . The summit air is thin enough that people who felt fine in town get lightheaded, so go easy up there.
Walk through the Manitou Cliff Dwellings Just west of town on Highway 24, this privately owned site lets you walk through and touch Ancestral Puebloan stonework , which you cannot do at Mesa Verde. Worth knowing before you go: the dwellings were not built here. Stonework was moved from McElmo Canyon near Mesa Verde between 1904 and 1907 and reassembled at this spot, which opened to the public in 1907. Ancestral Puebloan peoples lived in the Four Corners region, several hundred miles southwest. Going in with that context makes it a more interesting visit, not a worse one.
As of 2026, it is open daily from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., extending to 6 p.m. in good weather. Admission runs about $12.75 for adults, $10 for seniors, and $8 for children, plus tax.
Kit Leong – stock.adobe.com Soak at SunWater Spa Manitou has no natural hot springs, but SunWater Spa at 514 El Paso Boulevard draws water from 7 Minute Spring, heats it on site, and fills twelve private cedar tubs across three outdoor levels. Tubs run 99 to 104 degrees, and a 90-minute reservation also gets you an indoor saline pool, two cold plunges, and a sauna.
Browse downtown and the galleries Downtown is a few walkable blocks of Victorian storefronts housing galleries, bookshops, rock and mineral stores, vintage clothing shops, and candy shops. The Manitou Art Center anchors the arts scene with gallery space, a maker space for digital artists, and classes. Murals and street art fill the alleys and change often enough that walking the same blocks twice a year turns up new work. There is a mineral spring roughly every other block if you need a drink along the way.
Come for the Emma Crawford Coffin Races Emma Crawford arrived in 1889 hoping the mineral water would cure her tuberculosis. She died in 1891, and her dying wish was to be buried atop Red Mountain. Her fiancé, a Cog Railway engineer, carried her coffin up with eleven other townspeople. In 1929, the mountainside gave way, and Emma came back down it. Children found the casket handles, a nameplate, and a few bones.
Photo_Hiker_Dave – Flickr In 1995, the Chamber of Commerce turned this into the first coffin races in the country. Teams build wheeled coffins, each carrying an Emma, and race them down Manitou Avenue every October in front of thousands. It is the busiest weekend of the year, so book lodging early.
Getting There and Parking Highway 24 runs along the northern edge of town and is how nearly everyone arrives, whether from Colorado Springs fifteen minutes east or from the mountains to the west. Denver is about 70 miles north. The nearest airport is Colorado Springs, roughly 20 miles away.
Parking is the thing first-time visitors underestimate. It is paid from 7 a.m. to 6 p.m. and free after that, which makes dinner downtown cheaper than lunch. Downtown runs about $2 per hour in summer and $1.50 in winter, with a $0.40 processing fee. Rates outside the core climb steeply for long stays.
The single best piece of advice here: park once downtown and take the free #33 shuttle. It runs every 20 minutes from 6 a.m. to 8 p.m. and connects downtown to the Cog Depot and the Incline base, which means you never have to drive on Ruxton Avenue. It is narrow, residential, and has almost no parking. The shuttle will not run up Ruxton in bad weather, so check conditions in winter.
When to Visit Ning Goldtranquil – Flickr Fall is the best window. September and October bring cool air, turning aspens, and the town at its most photogenic. The exception is Coffin Race weekend in late October, when Manitou is as busy as it gets.
Summer means warm days, the biggest crowds, and near-daily afternoon thunderstorms, which matter most on the Incline or the Pikes Peak summit. Get high-elevation plans done in the morning. Winter is quiet, cheaper, and underrated, though the Barr Trail descent ices up and traction spikes become necessary. Spring is unpredictable, with late snow common well into May at this elevation.
Whenever you come, the altitude is real. Town sits around 6,300 feet and the Pikes Peak summit is over 14,000. Drink more water than usual and take your first day easy.
Flickr Mike McBey Where to Eat and Stay For a town this size, the food is a genuine draw, with more than 30 locally owned restaurants within three miles and very little chain presence in the historic district. The best-documented option is the dining room at The Cliff House at Pikes Peak , a AAA Four Diamond restaurant that has held the rating since 2001 and features a wine list of over 700 selections. The Queen’s Parlor Tearoom is another long-runner, serving high tea.
Staying in town rather than in Colorado Springs is worth the premium if you want to walk to the springs and reach the Incline base early. The Cliff House is a landmark property and a Historic Hotels of America member, housed in a building that predates Colorado statehood.
Nearby Day Trips John Hoffman – stock.adobe.com Manitou works as a base for the whole Pikes Peak region. Garden of the Gods is five minutes away and free to enter. Cave of the Winds sits just up Highway 24 in Williams Canyon; downtown Colorado Springs is fifteen minutes east for a bigger dinner scene, and Cripple Creek, a former gold rush town turned small casino district, is about an hour west over Ute Pass.
Manitou Springs FAQs What is Manitou Springs known for? It’s eight free naturally carbonated mineral springs, the Manitou Incline, a penny arcade running since 1933, and its arts scene. The town was founded in 1888 as a health resort built around the spring water.
How do you spend a day in Manitou Springs? Hike the Incline early if you are up for it, walk the mineral springs loop downtown late morning, eat lunch on Manitou Avenue, spend the afternoon in the Penny Arcade and the galleries, then soak at SunWater Spa. Swap the Incline for the Cog Railway or the Cliff Dwellings if you would rather not climb.
Are the Manitou Springs hot springs? No. They are cold and naturally carbonated, emerging at ground temperature rather than geothermal temperature. SunWater Spa heats Manitou mineral water on site for soaking, but there is no natural hot spring in town.
Is parking free in Manitou Springs? Not during the day. Paid parking runs from 7 a.m. to 6 p.m. downtown, at roughly $2 per hour in summer and $1.50 in winter, and is free after 6 p.m. The #33 shuttle is free and connects downtown to the Incline area.
How far is Manitou Springs from Colorado Springs? About six miles, roughly fifteen minutes by car on Highway 24. Denver is about 70 miles north.
